Note: Niantic primarily assesses content (including illegal content) for violations by reference to its policies. Any content that is actioned on the basis of the law also is taken on the basis of the terms and conditions of the service, because all illegal content is also policy-violating, therefore the numbers reported on "5_own_initiative_illegal" and overlap and are repeated (not in addition to) the numbers reported on "6_own_initiative_TC".
column23: The only content moderation process that is entirely automated for Pokémon GO is when a Route fails our location classifier. A Pokémon GO Route is a path that players can follow to explore their local area. Routes can be created by Niantic, official partners or other players. If the classifiers identify a Route to be an unsafe, inaccessible, or private location as determined by our location classifier, the Route will be auto-rejected. Upon rejection, a user receives a notification that contains the reason why the Route was rejected. If a Route is rejected, a user also has the opportunity to appeal that decision.  More information about Routes can be found in the Help Center: https://niantic.helpshift.com/hc/en/6-pokemon-go/faq/4175-what-are-routes/.
